title: Measurement of Tension Release During Laser Induced Axon Lesion to Evaluate Axonal Adhesion to the Substrate at Piconewton and Millisecond Resolution
protocol: Maintain the temperature of the cell culture under the microscope at 37°C using a Peltier device.
Aerate a custom-designed PDMS sleeve integrating the microscope objective with humidified carbogen (95% O2, 5% CO2) to maintain pH and humidity in the culture.
Obtain primary cultures from hippocampi of E18 mice.
Plate neurons at a concentration of 25,000 cells/ml on glass-bottom Petri dishes.
Coat polymer microspheres with poly-D-lysine following the procedure described in the polyLink Protein Coupling Kit.
Choose an isolated neuron for experimentation.
Detach a bead from the culture substrate.
Trap and move the bead next to the chosen neuron.
Put the culture Petri dish on the microscope stage.
Set the focus on the sample by moving the stage.
Correct the position of the illuminating objective condenser to set Kohler-illumination.
Pipette a few μl of the coated microsphere stock solution into the culture dish.
Turn on the IR trapping laser.
Set the axial position of the IR spot 2-3 μm above the culture support surface by moving the microscope stage.
Set the UV laser power to less than 1 μW.
Move the UV spot above the adhered bead using microscope stage motion.
Turn off the UV laser once the bead detaches from the surface and is trapped by the IR laser.
Move the trapped bead several micrometers (20-30 μm) above the glass support.
Set the stage speed to a low value (10 μm/sec).
Move the bead toward the previously chosen neuron.
Bring the bead to the position of the axon being visualized.
Hold the bead about 5 μm above the glass support to avoid contact with cells.
Move the microscope stage to place the UV focus spot at the center of the width of the axon.
Save the current stage position.
Project a computer-generated hologram to move the IR focus spot position.
Stop the stage in the previously chosen position.
Position the trapped bead on the center of the neurite by moving the IR laser spot.
Center the UV laser spot on the same neurite as the trapped bead.
Place the IR spot and thus the trapped bead along the neurite 5-10 μm away from the UV spot.
Adjust the IR spot position with respect to the UV spot based on the neurite geometry.
Position the IR spot 5-10 μm away from the UV spot if an SLM system is not available.
Avoid optical interaction between the dissecting beam and the trapped probe to prevent altering force spectroscopy traces.
Move the stage to place the trapped bead away from the axon to avoid collision.
Adjust the axial position of the trapped bead to approximately 2 μm above the cover glass.
Align the QPD to center the interference fringes on it: x and y QPD differential signals are zeros when the QPD is centered.
Acquire 5 sec of the Brownian motion of the trapped bead by the interferometer at 50 KHz sampling rate.
Obtain the stiffness (pN/nm) and sensitivity (V/nm) of the optical trap by the power spectrum method.
Raise the trapped bead position about 4 μm above the cover glass, and move it to the previously saved stage position.
Move the trapped bead down toward the axon until it contacts the neurite.
Wait 10 sec with the trapped bead pushed against the axon to favor its adhesion to the neurite membrane.
Move the micro stage to displace the trapped bead from the axon, and thus verify its adhesion to the cell membrane.
Move back the laser trap on the adhered bead.
Switch on the force-clamp loop with force condition equal to zero.
Reposition the bead attached to the cell on the optical trap center using the piezo-stage.
If the system does not have a feedback loop control, move the laser trap position by the microscope stage to center it on the adhered probe.
Reach the center of the trap when QPD signals are the same as when the bead is trapped and not adhered to the cell (x and y QPD signals equal to zero).
Set a force-clamp condition on the z axis, positioning the trapping laser slightly over the center of the bead (about 100 nm) to generate pretension.
If the system lacks a force-clamp control, raise the optical trap position in steps of 25 nm by the microscope stage.
Monitor the z QPD signal to set the position of the laser trap with respect to the adhered probe.
Use pre-tension to sense strain on the membrane after axonal lesion and consequent decrease of Brownian motion of the adhered probe.
Switch-off the force-clamp feedback to measure the force on the adhered probe in the position-clamp condition.
Start simultaneous recording of the trapped probe positions through the interferometer at 20 KHz sampling frequency.
Record cell during laser axotomy time-lapse bright-field imaging at 20 Hz frame rate.
Turn on the UV laser to deliver laser pulses until a lesion becomes visible on the image of the axon.
Continue delivering laser pulses (usually 200-400 optical pulses, energy per pulse: 25 nJ).
Turn off the UV laser after lesion visibility.
Continue recording by the interferometer for about 3 min until x, y and z QPD traces reach a plateau.
Filter x, y, and z displacement traces by a high pass filter with a cutoff at 10 Hz.
Calculate the total variance of the filtered traces representing the Brownian motion of the trapped bead.
Calculate the variance at 25 msec steps for overlapping time windows of 500 msec (10,000 data points).
Define t0 as the beginning of the decrease in the Brownian motion variance after the delivery of UV laser energy.
Define t1 as the end of the decrease in the Brownian motion variance when it reaches a plateau.
Perform video tracking of debris or a scratch on the cover glass support to measure any drift of the sample during force measurement.
Apply thresholds to bright-field images to obtain a stack of binary images with the particle in white on a black background.
Track the particle center of mass with sub-pixel accuracy using ImageJ software.
Subtract the measured drift from the displacement QPD traces.
Multiply the drift-corrected QPD traces by the respective calibrated optical stiffness (kx, ky, kz) to obtain the Fx, Fy, Fz traces in piconewtons.
Calculate the total force trace as Ftot = √(Fx²+Fy²+Fz²).
Calculate the total release of force between t0 and t1 as Freleased= Ftot(t1) - Ftot(t0).
Measure the long (L) and short (D) axes of the neurite between the trapped bead and the UV laser spot position.
Calculate the axon contact area as Aaxon = L x D.
Normalize the total released force Freleased by the axon contact area Aaxon.
